# RFC-0008: Playbook calls

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Will Eaton

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0008:C-SCOPE] Scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0008c-scope"></a>

A playbook can start a run of another pipeline and use what that run returns. The task that does this is a call. Its target is another Crucible playbook or a pipeline on an external system: a GitHub Actions workflow, a GitLab pipeline, or a Tekton pipeline. The target runs as its own run, not as part of the caller's graph. The caller binds the target's inputs from its own task outputs, agent or command alike, including JSON values and files, and receives the target's result as the call's output.

A playbook can also wait for the pipelines a commit started without starting them. The task that does this is a watch. It matches the runs a target's system records for a commit, such as the Pipelines-as-Code PipelineRuns or the GitLab pipelines a push or pull request triggered, waits until they end, and returns their results. Both tasks reach target systems only through the controller, and the engine holds no credential for them.

This RFC covers the call and watch tasks in the workflow DSL; how a pack names and pins its targets; the JSON and file parameter types a target can declare; how the controller dispatches, finds, follows, and cancels target runs; and how a client draws one. It does not cover a target that runs inside the caller's run, a call that does not wait for its target, or parking a waiting caller.

The parameter types in [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-param-types) extend [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params), and call and watch are engine-owned tasks under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape). Finalizing this RFC requires amending both.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0008:C-CALL] The call task (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-call"></a>

A playbook or custom workflow MAY declare a call task with call(). A call takes a name, a target, params, and optionally over, budget, depends_on, required, join, stage, and when, with the meanings [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape) and the DSL reference give them on any task. An autoresearch workflow MUST NOT declare one.

target MUST name a target the source's calls block declares ([RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets)). The engine MUST refuse a target that the block does not declare.

params MUST be a dict from the target's declared parameter names to values. A value MUST be one of:

- a literal of the parameter's type;
- param(name), a parameter of the calling workflow;
- producer.field, a field a dependency of the call declares in emits; or
- producer.files[path], a path a dependency of the call declares in emits_files.

A producer MUST be a direct dependency of the call. The engine MUST check every binding against the target's interface in the call lock ([RFC-0008:C-LOCK](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-lock)) at compile time and MUST refuse a source in which a required target parameter is unbound, a name is not a target parameter, a field's declared type does not match the parameter's type, or a file is bound to a parameter that is not a file parameter. A field typed by a schema MUST match only a json parameter, and the parameter's schema, when it has one, MUST be equal to the field's.

over = each(producer.field, max = N) MUST make the call a mapped task: one target run per item, with item available as a value in params. The engine MUST refuse N above 64.

The engine MUST bind every value when the call becomes ready, not at compile time. A value the target refuses, such as one outside a choice set or a pattern, MUST settle the call failing with the refusal as its note before any target run is created and without spend.

A call task's output MUST be the target's result as [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets) defines it, typed by the target's interface, so that dependents, when, and route decisions read it as they read any task's output. The target's result files MUST be staged as the call's declared files under [RFC-0002:C-TASK-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-task-files).

A call MUST settle passing when the target run ends passing, failing when it ends failing, timed out, or cancelled by anything other than its caller, with the target's own note, and cancelled when its caller is cancelled. A call task MUST NOT set complete. A call MUST NOT be a member of a revise loop body or a session.

### [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS] Call targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-targets"></a>

A workflow source MAY declare the targets it calls or watches in a calls block: an assignment to calls that comes before every statement but the params block of [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params), whose value is a dictionary literal from a target name to a dictionary literal built only from dictionaries, lists, strings, numbers, and booleans. The engine and the controller MUST be able to read the block without evaluating the source, MUST refuse a calls assignment anywhere else, and MUST refuse a block that is not such a literal. A target name MUST be unique in the block and every target MUST carry a kind. The engine and the controller MUST refuse a target whose kind they do not implement. They MUST implement the kinds "playbook" and "github_workflow", and MAY implement "gitlab_pipeline" and "tekton". A manifest MUST NOT declare call targets.

A "playbook" target MUST name a playbook by its registered name, or by a draft the pack's owner may read. A "github_workflow" target MUST name a repo as owner/name, a workflow file path under .github/workflows, a ref that is a branch or tag, and the outputs [RFC-0008:C-GITHUB-WORKFLOW](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-github-workflow) reads. A "gitlab_pipeline" target MUST carry the fields [RFC-0008:C-GITLAB-PIPELINE](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-gitlab-pipeline) gives it, and a "tekton" target those [RFC-0008:C-TEKTON](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-tekton) gives it.

For each kind the controller MUST implement these operations, and the engine MUST NOT perform any of them itself:

- interface: the target's parameters as a schema of the types [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) and [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-param-types) admit; its result as the fields and files it declares; and its static graph as [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress) shapes it.
- dispatch, for a kind and declaration that can start runs: start one target run with bound values and return a handle that identifies it on its system.
- find, for a kind and declaration that can watch: the runs the target's system records for a commit, each with its name and handle ([RFC-0008:C-WATCH](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-watch)).
- progress: a target run's current graph as [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress) shapes it.
- outcome: once a target run ends, its status, its note, its result fields, and its result files.
- cancel: stop a target run that a dispatch started.

The engine MUST refuse at compile time a call whose target's declaration lacks the fields its kind needs to dispatch, naming the task and the target. One declaration MAY carry the fields for both and serve a call and a watch. Progress and outcome MUST read a run a find matched as they read a run a dispatch started.

For a "playbook" target, the interface MUST be the target pack's params block, its workflow result task's emits and emits_files, and its compiled graph; the outcome MUST be its result task's output and files, and its status the run's verdict. A target playbook that declares no result MUST have an empty result.

### [RFC-0008:C-LOCK] Call lock (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-lock"></a>

A pack any of whose workflow sources declares a calls block MUST hold a lock file, calls.lock, at its root. One lock serves every workflow source the manifest names, its variants' included, and two sources that give one target name different targets MUST be refused. For each target name the lock MUST record the target's kind, its pin, and its interface as [RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets) defines it, with the digest of the interface. The lock is a pack file, so the pack's digest under [RFC-0002:C-PACK-BASE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-pack-base) covers it, and approving a pack approves its pins.

A pin MUST be one of:

- the digest of a registered playbook's revision;
- a draft's head, which only a draft pack MAY pin, resolved at dispatch to the draft's latest saved version that compiles; or
- for a GitHub workflow or GitLab pipeline, the repository, the workflow path for GitHub, and the ref, with the commit the ref named when the lock was written;
- for a Tekton pipeline, the bundle digest, or the Pipeline's uid and generation; or
- for a target only watches use, no pin.

The controller MUST write the lock when it saves a draft version, and MUST refuse to save, register, or import a pack whose lock is missing, names a target no workflow source declares, omits one a source declares, or records an interface that differs from what the target's interface operation returns for its pin at that time. A crucible command MUST be able to write the lock for a pack in a source repository, given a controller.

The engine MUST check, before compiling anything else, that the lock pins every target its source declares, and MUST compile a call against the lock alone. It MUST NOT contact a target's system to compile, and a compile MUST NOT need the result of another compile.

A pin that moves, a draft head or a git ref, MUST be resolved again at dispatch. The controller MUST refuse to dispatch a target whose interface at dispatch differs from the locked interface, and the call MUST settle failing with a note naming the target and the difference, before any target run is created. A registered pin MUST NOT be resolved again. The controller MUST refuse to register or import a pack whose lock pins a draft head.

A target only watches use MUST be locked with its declared filters, expected names, and results as its interface, and MUST NOT be resolved again or refused for drift when a watch starts. A watch reads the runs a commit started, whose definitions are those at that commit, not at any pin.

### [RFC-0008:C-PARAM-TYPES] JSON and file parameters (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-param-types"></a>

A declared parameter MAY have type json or file, in addition to the types [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) lists.

A json parameter's value MUST be a JSON object or array of at most 64 KiB serialized. Its declaration MAY name schema, a path below the pack directory to a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) read under the rules schema_file() follows. A launch MUST be refused when the value does not validate against the schema. A json parameter MUST NOT take choices, choices_from, pattern, or multiline.

A file parameter's value MUST be one file of at most max_bytes, which the declaration MUST set and which MUST NOT exceed 16 MiB. Its declaration MAY name media_type, a list of media types the file must have. The controller MUST store a supplied file as a blob owned by the launch, record its digest and size with the launch, and deliver it beside the pack's tree, never inside it. A file parameter MUST NOT take a default or any value constraint other than max_bytes and media_type.

A command or evaluate task MUST receive a json parameter's value under params as JSON, and a file parameter as an object giving the staged file's path, size, digest, and media type. An agent task MUST receive a json value only inside a region marked as external input, as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-PARAMS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-params) requires, and a file only as a read-only staged input under the same marking; a json value MUST NOT be convertible to plain text, as a string parameter is not.

A launch form MUST take a json parameter as text validated against its schema before submission, and a file parameter as an upload refused above max_bytes. The JSON Schema the engine emits for the params block MUST describe both, with the schema embedded for json.

### [RFC-0008:C-CHILD-RUN] Target runs (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-child-run"></a>

When a call becomes ready, the engine MUST ask the controller to dispatch its target, authenticated as its own run, and MUST then wait inside the call's own execution until the controller reports the target run ended. The caller's wall-clock ceiling MUST keep running while it waits.

The controller MUST identify a target run by the calling run, the call task, the mapped instance, and the attempt, and MUST create at most one target run per identity. The engine MUST record the target run's handle in the session log before it waits. A resumed caller MUST attach to the target run its handle names and MUST NOT dispatch a second one, and the target run MUST NOT be cancelled by its caller's interruption alone.

A "playbook" target run MUST be a run of its own, with its own run identity, pack, manifest, sandbox, secrets, and dispatch target, and MUST record the calling run, call task, and instance as its parent. It MUST be launched with the authority of the calling run's launch owner under [RFC-0003:C-DECISION](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-decision): the controller MUST refuse to dispatch it, and the call MUST settle failing, when that owner may not launch the target at its pin.

A target run's cost and wall-clock ceilings MUST NOT be drawn from the caller's. A call MAY set budget = budget(cost = ..., wall_clock = ...), and the target run's ceilings MUST then be those values, bounded by what the controller allows a launch of that target. Otherwise they MUST be the ceilings the controller gives a manual launch of the target. The caller's spend MUST NOT include the target run's. For a target that has no cost, wall_clock MUST still bound it: the controller MUST cancel the target run when it is exceeded, and the call MUST settle failing.

Cancelling a calling run MUST cancel every target run it dispatched that has not ended. A target run MUST NOT dispatch a call when it is already the fourth in a chain of calling runs, and the call MUST settle failing. The controller MUST refuse to dispatch a playbook target whose playbook is the playbook of any run in the chain of calling runs above it, the calling run's own included, and the call MUST settle failing with a note naming the chain. The engine MUST refuse a source whose calls block names, as a playbook target, the playbook the source belongs to.

The controller MUST record, for each target run, the bound values it dispatched with, file digests in place of file contents, so that what left the calling run is auditable.

### [RFC-0008:C-GITHUB-WORKFLOW] GitHub workflow targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-github-workflow"></a>

A "github_workflow" target's interface MUST be read from the workflow file at the pinned commit: its parameters from on.workflow_dispatch.inputs, where string, choice, and environment inputs are string parameters, a boolean input is a boolean parameter, and a number input is a number parameter; and its static graph from its jobs and their needs. Its result MUST be the outputs the manifest entry declares: the name of an artifact the workflow uploads, the fields of a JSON object at result.json in that artifact, and the paths of further files in it. The controller MUST refuse a workflow file that has no workflow_dispatch trigger or more inputs than GitHub accepts.

A json parameter of a call MUST be bound to a string input and sent as its serialized JSON. A file parameter MUST NOT be bound to a GitHub workflow input, and the engine MUST refuse a lock or source that does.

The controller MUST dispatch with the token of the GitHub App installation on the target repository, and MUST refuse a target whose repository the App is not installed on or whose installation lacks actions write permission. It MUST dispatch on the pinned ref, MUST request the created run's details, and MUST use the run identifier GitHub returns as the handle. It MUST NOT find the run by searching recent runs. It MUST record the head commit the run ran on.

The controller SHOULD learn progress from verified workflow_run and workflow_job deliveries under [RFC-0003:C-WEBHOOK-DELIVERY](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-webhook-delivery) and MUST also poll the run and its jobs, so that a lost delivery delays the outcome but cannot lose it.

A completed run's conclusion MUST map as follows: success to passing; failure, timed_out, startup_failure, action_required, and stale to failing; cancelled to failing unless the caller cancelled it; skipped and neutral to passing with an empty result. A passing run whose declared artifact or result.json is missing, unreadable, or does not match the declared fields MUST settle the call failing with a note naming what is missing.

### [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS] Target progress (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-progress"></a>

For every target kind, the controller MUST describe a target's static graph and a target run's progress in one shape: a list of nodes and a list of edges between them. A node MUST carry an identifier unique within the graph, a label, and a status; and MAY carry a group, start and end times, a kind-specific detail, and a link. The status MUST be one of the task statuses a Crucible run's graph uses, so that one renderer draws every kind, and each kind MUST state its mapping.

For a "playbook" target, nodes MUST be the target run's tasks and their mapped instances, with the run's own statuses, and a node's link MUST name the target run and task. For a "github_workflow" target, nodes MUST be its jobs, with matrix legs of one job in one group and edges from needs; a node's detail MUST list the job's steps with their status and times, and its link MUST be the job's page on GitHub. A "gitlab_pipeline" target's nodes are those [RFC-0008:C-GITLAB-PIPELINE](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-gitlab-pipeline) gives it, and a "tekton" target's those [RFC-0008:C-TEKTON](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-tekton) gives it. Before dispatch, the static graph from the lock MUST be served with every node pending.

A watch's progress MUST be one group per matched run, named by the run's name and holding that run's nodes, with no edges between groups. Before the first run matches, the controller MUST serve the static graph the lock records for each expected name, with every node pending, and MUST replace each with the matched run's own nodes.

The controller MUST serve the progress of every target run a run dispatched or watched to whoever may read the calling run, and MUST NOT serve to a reader of the calling run anything else of a playbook target run that the reader may not read under [RFC-0003:C-READ-SCOPING](../rfc/RFC-0003.md#rfc-0003c-read-scoping): such a node MUST show its label and status and no link. The controller MUST bound a progress graph at 512 nodes and say how many it left out.

### [RFC-0008:C-VIEW] Drawing calls (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-view"></a>

A client that draws a run's graph MUST draw a call task as a node distinct from other task kinds, labelled with its alias and target kind, and MUST let a reader expand it into the target's graph from [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress), drawn inside a frame attached to the call's place in the caller's graph. A mapped call MUST draw one frame per instance and fold them as other mapped tasks fold. An edge into a call SHOULD be labelled with the parameter it binds.

From an expanded call, a reader MUST be able to open a node's link: a node of a playbook target opens that task in the target run, and a node of an external target opens its page outside the client. The call node MUST also open the target run as a whole. A client showing a playbook run that a call dispatched MUST show the calling run and call task and open them, so that a reader can move from caller to target and back.

A client MUST draw a watch task as a node distinct from a call, labelled with its alias, target kind, and the short commit it watches, and MUST let a reader expand it into a frame holding one group per matched run, each foldable, and each opening its run on the target's system. A frame MUST show, while the appearance window is open, that more runs may still appear.

A client that lists runs SHOULD list a run a call dispatched under the run that called it rather than beside it.

A client that previews a pack's graph before launch MUST draw each call's static graph from the lock.

### [RFC-0008:C-WATCH] The watch task (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-watch"></a>

A playbook or custom workflow MAY declare a watch task with watch(). A watch takes a name, a target, a commit, and a timeout, and optionally appear, depends_on, required, join, stage, and when, with the meanings [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape) and the DSL reference give them on any task. A watch MUST NOT take params, over, or budget. An autoresearch workflow MUST NOT declare one.

target MUST name a target the calls block declares ([RFC-0008:C-TARGETS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-targets)) whose kind can find runs and whose declaration carries the fields its kind needs to find them. The kinds that can find runs are "tekton" and "gitlab_pipeline". The engine MUST refuse any other watch target at compile time, from the calls block and the lock alone, naming the task and the target. commit MUST be a literal string, param(name), or producer.field of a direct dependency whose declared type is string. The engine MUST bind it when the watch becomes ready, and MUST settle the watch failing before it asks the controller anything when the value is not a full commit identifier of 40 or 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

timeout MUST be a duration of at most 24 hours. appear MUST be a duration no longer than timeout and defaults to 10 minutes. The engine MUST refuse a source that breaks either bound.

When a watch becomes ready, the engine MUST ask the controller, authenticated as its own run, to start the watch, and MUST then wait inside the watch's own execution until the controller reports it settled. The controller MUST identify a watch by the calling run, the task, and the attempt, and MUST create at most one watch per identity. A resumed caller MUST attach to the watch its identity names.

A target run matches a watch when the target's system records it as run for the watched commit and it passes every filter the target declares. Each matched run MUST carry a name its kind defines. The appearance window opens when the watch starts and closes appear later. The controller MUST add each matching run to the watch's matched set when it first sees it while the window is open. After the window closes, the set MUST NOT gain a name it did not hold, and a run under a name it holds MUST replace the earlier run only when the target's system records it as a later attempt for the same commit.

The watch MUST settle:

- failing, when the window closes and the set is empty or lacks a name the target declares as expected, with a note naming what is missing;
- failing, as soon as any matched run ends failing, with that run's name and note;
- passing, once the window has closed and every matched run ended passing;
- failing, at timeout, with a note naming the matched runs that had not ended; and
- cancelled, when its caller is cancelled.

A watch MUST NOT cancel any target run. Settling, timing out, and the caller's cancellation or interruption MUST leave every matched run as it was.

A watch's output MUST be an object with a field runs, a list giving each matched run's name, handle, status, and link, and one field per expected name the target declares, holding the results the target declares for that run, typed as the call lock records them ([RFC-0008:C-LOCK](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-lock)). A result the target declares that the ended run does not carry MUST settle the watch failing with a note naming it. A watch MUST NOT declare emits_files.

A watch MUST NOT set complete, and MUST NOT be a member of a revise loop body or a session. The controller MUST serve a watch's progress as [RFC-0008:C-PROGRESS](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-progress) shapes it, with one group per matched run.

### [RFC-0008:C-GITLAB-PIPELINE] GitLab pipeline targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-gitlab-pipeline"></a>

A "gitlab_pipeline" target MUST name host, an HTTPS GitLab instance the controller is configured to reach, and project, the project's full path. Dispatch MUST also need ref, a branch or tag, and outputs, read as [RFC-0008:C-GITHUB-WORKFLOW](../rfc/RFC-0008.md#rfc-0008c-github-workflow) reads them except that it names a job whose artifacts hold result.json rather than an artifact. Find MAY use sources, a list of pipeline sources such as push or merge_request_event, and MAY use expected, a list of the sources the watch waits for, each optionally with outputs.

A dispatch target's interface MUST be read from the project's CI configuration at the pinned commit. Its parameters MUST be the spec:inputs of the configuration's header: a string input is a string parameter, with its options as a choice set and its regex as a pattern; a number input is a number parameter; a boolean input is a boolean parameter; and an array input is a list of strings when its default is one, and a json parameter otherwise. A configuration with no spec:inputs MUST have no parameters, and the controller MUST NOT bind parameters to CI variables. Its static graph MUST be the jobs GitLab reports when it validates the configuration for the pinned ref without creating a pipeline, with stages as groups and edges from needs, or from stage order for a job with no needs. Its pin MUST record the host, project, ref, and the commit the ref named.

The controller MUST dispatch by creating a pipeline on the pinned ref with the bound values as inputs, and MUST use the pipeline identifier the create returns as the handle. It MUST NOT find the pipeline by searching. It MUST record the commit the pipeline runs on. A json parameter bound to a string input MUST be sent as its serialized JSON. A file parameter MUST NOT be bound to a GitLab input.

Find MUST list the project's pipelines whose commit is the watched commit and whose source is among sources when the target names them. A matched pipeline's name MUST be its source. A later pipeline for the same commit and source MUST be the later attempt.

A node MUST be one job or trigger job of the pipeline, grouped by stage, with edges from needs. A trigger job's node MUST name the downstream pipeline in its detail and MUST NOT be expanded into it. Job statuses MUST map: created, waiting_for_resource, preparing, pending, scheduled, and manual to pending; running to running; success to pass; failed to fail, or pass with a note when the job allows failure; canceled to fail; and skipped to skipped.

A pipeline's status MUST map: success to passing; failed to failing; canceled to failing unless the caller cancelled it; skipped to passing with an empty result; and manual, a pipeline blocked on a manual job, to failing with a note naming the job. A passing pipeline whose declared job, artifact, or result.json is missing or does not match the declared fields MUST settle failing with a note naming what is missing.

Cancel MUST cancel the pipeline. The controller SHOULD learn progress from pipeline and job webhook deliveries it can verify, and MUST also poll.

The controller's own credential on a host MUST be a token of a bot user or an access token of a project or group that the operator binds to that host. On a controller that runs for one person on their machine, the credential MAY instead be that person's own token for the host, held in memory only. A dispatch MUST fail with a note when the credential's own access level on the project is below Developer, and a find when it is below Reporter. A job node MUST carry the host, project, and job identifier, from which a client reads the job's log.

### [RFC-0008:C-TEKTON] Tekton pipeline targets (Normative) <a id="rfc-0008c-tekton"></a>

A "tekton" target MUST name cluster, a cluster the controller knows by name, and namespace. Dispatch MUST also need repo, an HTTPS git repository, path, a PipelineRun file in its .tekton directory, and ref, a branch or tag. Dispatch MAY also use git_auth_secret, the name of a Secret in the namespace that stands for the per-run git credentials Pipelines-as-Code would otherwise create. Find MUST also need repository, the name of the Pipelines-as-Code Repository the runs belong to, and MAY use event, push or pull_request, and expected, a list of the PipelineRun names the watch waits for, each optionally with results, a list of the Tekton result names the watch returns for it.

A dispatch target's interface MUST be read from the PipelineRun file at the pinned commit. Its parameters MUST be the file's spec.params, each with the file's value as its default: a string value is a string parameter and an array value a list of strings. Its result MUST be the results the target declares, each a string field. Its static graph MUST be the tasks and finally tasks of the file's embedded pipelineSpec, finally tasks in one group, with edges from runAfter and from one task's reference to another's results; a file that references its pipeline by pipelineRef MUST have no static graph until a run resolves it. Its pin MUST record the repo, path, ref, and the commit the ref named. A find-only target MUST have no parameters, its result MUST be the results it names under expected, each as a string field, and it MUST have no static graph.

The controller MUST dispatch by creating a PipelineRun in the namespace from the file at the pinned commit: with the Pipelines-as-Code variables the file uses for its revision, repository URL, owner, name, and branches set from the pin; with its Pipelines-as-Code annotations removed, so that no Pipelines-as-Code controller acts on it; with the bound values as its params; and labelled with the calling run, the call, the instance, and the attempt. The controller MUST set git_auth_secret from the target's declaration, and MUST refuse a file that uses a Pipelines-as-Code variable it cannot set from the pin or the declaration, naming the variable. It MUST use the namespace and name the create returns as the handle. Before it creates a PipelineRun for an attempt whose earlier create may have been lost, it MUST look for one already carrying that attempt's labels and use it. A json or file parameter MUST NOT be bound to a Tekton param.

Find MUST list the PipelineRuns in the namespace that Pipelines-as-Code labels with the watched commit and with the target's repository, and with the event type when the target names one. A matched run's name MUST be the PipelineRun name Pipelines-as-Code labels as its original name, and otherwise the PipelineRun's own name. Of two runs under one name, the one created later MUST be the later attempt.

A node MUST be one pipeline task or finally task of the run's resolved pipeline spec, with its TaskRun's status, its steps with their status and times as its detail, and the TaskRun's pod with one container per step, from which a client reads the step's log. A node's link MUST be the log address Pipelines-as-Code annotates on the run when it does. Statuses MUST map: no TaskRun yet, or a TaskRun not started, to pending; a TaskRun whose Succeeded condition is Unknown to running; True to pass; False to fail; and a task the run reports as skipped to skipped.

A PipelineRun's Succeeded condition MUST map: True to passing; False with a cancellation reason to failing unless the caller cancelled it; False for any other reason, a timeout included, to failing with the condition's message as its note. Its result fields MUST be read from the run's results. A declared result the ended run does not carry MUST settle failing with a note naming it.

A run the cluster deletes before the controller saw it end MUST be read from the cluster's Tekton Results record when the cluster records one, and otherwise MUST settle failing with a note saying the run was pruned before it ended.

Cancel MUST set the PipelineRun's status to CancelledRunFinally. The controller MUST poll, and MAY watch the API.

The controller MUST act on a cluster with a token bound to that cluster: a service account token the operator binds, or, on a controller that runs for one person on their machine, that person's own token for the cluster, held in memory only. A client MAY read a run's PipelineRuns, TaskRuns, and step logs from the cluster's API directly with the reader's own token for the cluster, and MUST fall back to the controller's progress when it holds none or the read fails. The controller MUST refuse a dispatch when its token may not create PipelineRuns in the namespace, and a find when it may not list them, with a note naming the namespace.
